synthesis.description: Managers and senior staff arrange training for their people: system classes on SAP and the trading systems, a pilot programme, communication and ethics courses, cross-training on the desk and sit-ins with experienced colleagues. A round starts with a request to attend or an announcement of a class; the organiser asks managers to nominate or sign up staff, arranges cover such as night-shift staff arriving early, sets times and meetings, and prepares material or exercises. Approvals are sometimes given in a system that can fail.
steps: A manager, trainer or employee proposes a class, session or sit-in.
The organiser announces the session and asks managers to nominate attendees.
Managers rank or choose staff and send their names to sign up.
Shift cover is arranged so attendees can leave the desk.
The trainer prepares material, exercises or topics for the session.
The enrolment is approved, and the session is held and followed by later units.
synthesis.approach: Keep a shared training calendar with an online sign-up form: managers enter nominees, remaining seats show automatically, approvals route to the right manager, and confirmations and reminders go out without manual messages. A short checklist covers shift cover and preparation of materials.
synthesis.rationale: The rounds differ in subject but share the same arrangements: nominate, check seats, cover the desk, approve, prepare. A checklist helps the people organising sessions tomorrow; the sign-up form removes the repeated seat and enrolment questions seen in the mail.
